title: Find a Way
dateline: The Academy lawn. The same day.
mood: A head in her lap under a yellowing tree, one sentence about her father, and a paper nobody else has read.

hero.alt: Comic panel on a sunny lawn: pink-haired Guinevere lies on the grass with her head in Vexana's lap, grinning up, as Vexana's white glove rests on her hair and her other hand leans back on the grass.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 31

segs.t: At midday Guinevere lay down in the shade and put her head in Vexana’s lap. She did not ask first.
Vexana sat very still, her legs straight out on the grass, one hand back behind her. A head was heavier than she had thought. Pink hair spilled across her lap and out over the grass.
“You’re allowed to pat it,” said Guinevere. “Best partners. It’s the rules.”
“Which rules?”
“Mine. I just made them.”
Above them the tree was going yellow. Now and then a leaf let go and drifted down through the shade. Past its edge the lawn lay bright under a clear blue sky.
Guinevere’s two drones had come down in the grass beside them, round and still, ears folded. Asleep, Guinevere called it.
Their badges were still pinned on from the morning. Guinevere’s hung crooked below her star. Vexana had straightened one thing of hers today. She left the badge.
At the home nobody had touched anyone’s hair, except to cut it. Vexana lifted her hand and laid her glove on the pink hair, as lightly as she could.
“Was that a pat?” said Guinevere. “I didn’t feel a thing.”
Vexana patted harder. Guinevere’s head bounced in her lap.
“Ow! Careful! This head is famous now.”
“Since this morning.”
“Since this morning. It still counts.” Guinevere settled again. “Next year we win them again. And every year after, until they run out of badges.”
For once Vexana did not say
if
She tried the pat again, slower. Somewhere between too light and too hard, it came out right. Guinevere’s eyes half closed.
“There. Like that. Don’t stop.”
Vexana did not stop. For a while she did not count a single Ender in her head.
The light came down green and gold through the leaves. In her room, the white box on her desk held everything she had kept from the summer.
This won’t fit in the box,
she thought.
So she looked at it slowly, the leaves coming down and the pink hair under her glove.
Guinevere talked. One hand waved in the air above her face as she went, sketching the story on the leaves.
“Did I ever tell you about the wings?”
“No.”

“The day this place opened. The guards were shouting in the yard, so I ran out on our terrace.” Her hand swept across the branches. “And there they were. People flying over the hill on wings of light. A whole line of them, going down toward the water.”
“What did you do?”
“I pointed.” Her arm went straight up, as far as it would reach. “Like this. And I said, ‘That.’”
“That?”
“That. Hester knew exactly what I meant.”
“What did you mean?”
“That I wanted some.” She grinned up at Vexana, upside down. “And now I’ve got some. Ha.”
Her arm stayed up a moment longer.
Vexana looked where it pointed. Blue, between the yellow leaves. No stars in the daytime.
The wall stair came back to her. Her legs giving out halfway up, and her father carrying her the rest. At the top, the dark ground past the wall, and the stars over it.
“My father liked the stars,” she said.
Guinevere’s arm came down. “Who?”
“My father.”
Nothing came after it. Vexana had not known that one was coming.
Her hand had stopped on the pink hair. She could not make it move. She waited for the next question.
Where is he now?
The leaves moved overhead. Guinevere’s eyes went to the gold star at Vexana’s collar, and stayed there a moment.
The question did not come. Guinevere had promised once, on the grass by the training field, never to ask.
Instead her hand came up and found Vexana’s, on top of her own head. She patted it once.
He would have liked you,
thought Vexana.
Her legs had gone numb under the weight. She did not move them.
They stayed like that while the shade slid along the grass. After a while her hand began again. She had to learn how hard all over again.
Across the lawn the lunch bell rang. One drone’s ear flicked up, then folded again.
“Lunch,” said Vexana.
“Then we miss it,” said Guinevere, with her eyes shut. “Keep going.”
Vexana kept going.
A leaf landed on Guinevere’s nose. She blew it off.
“Want to hear something heroic?”
“No.”
“Teacher Chang’e told us,” said Guinevere, to the leaves, “to defeat the Will of the Planet, we must destroy The Enders’ Control Core hidden in its dark void.”
“But we can’t get near the void,” said Vexana.
Chang’e had said so herself. Nobody could.
Then she can’t go there either,
thought Vexana.
Guinevere sat bolt upright, so fast she nearly hit Vexana’s chin. Her eyes were squeezed shut, and she was grinning. Vexana’s hand was left in the air, half raised from the pat.

blocks.caption: Up so fast she nearly hit Vexana’s chin.

media.alt: Comic panel under a blue sky: black-haired Vexana says they can't get near the void, and Guinevere, popping up beside her with a wide grin, answers that she shouldn't worry.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 32

segs.t: “Don’t worry!”
Guinevere punched her fist out at the sky.
“I will definitely...” She held the pause. “...find a way...” Her eyes stayed shut. “...to destroy it!”
A leaf spun down past her knuckles.

She opened her eyes and thumped the badge on her chest. “Some Will in the dark sends claws at us, and thinks it gets to decide what happens next? It doesn’t.” She turned to Vexana. “We will decide the fate of the world ourselves.”
Vexana did not answer.
Her hand still hung in the air where Guinevere’s head had been.
That evening Vexana stood the frame on her desk, beside the white box.
In the picture they stood hand in hand with their heads turned to each other. Guinevere was grinning, as she always was. The black-haired girl beside her was smiling.
Before today, Vexana had never seen her own face do that.
Across the grounds the training hall’s windows lit. Guinevere, at her bag again. Later Vexana would phone and tell her to go to bed.
I will definitely find a way.
She means it,
thought Vexana.
If there is a way, she’ll be the first one through it.
Chang’e would not send a student anywhere she could not bring them back from. But nobody would have to send Guinevere.
Then I’ll find it first.
Vexana waited until the hall had been lit a while, long enough for Guinevere to lose herself in the bag. Then she went out by herself.
The library was empty at that hour, except for its droid at the front desk. It turned its one lens to her.
“Anything on the void,” said Vexana.
Its screen listed three papers. Two were old, and said less than Chang’e had said that morning.
The third bore Chang’e’s name.
On Aspirant Power and the Black Hole. A theory of the void. Status: untested.
The droid printed it for her. She took it to a table under a lamp and read the first page. Then she read it again.
Most of it was readings and numbers. One part was plain. Whatever fell into a black hole was torn apart, it said. The body went first.
Under that was one more line.
But an Aspirant’s light would shine on inside a black hole, and find its way home.
Her finger stopped on it, and stayed there.
